stem: In the Periodic Table, the p block contains elements whose outer electrons are found in the p subshell.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Elements in the p block show a general increase in first ionisation energy as the atomic number increases.
parts.text: Draw the shape of a p orbital.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation to show the first ionisation energy of silicon.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why there is a general increase in first ionisation energies of the elements across Period 3.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Element $\mathbf{A}$ is in the p block.

The graph shows the successive ionisation energies for the removal of the first ten electrons of $\mathbf{A}$.

{{figure:visual_auto_01.png}}

State and explain the group of the Periodic Table that element $\mathbf{A}$ belongs to.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Silicon is found in many compounds in the Earth's crust. Silicon has only three naturally occurring isotopes, $^{28}\text{Si}$, $^{29}\text{Si}$ and $^{30}\text{Si}$.
parts.text:
The table shows data for $^{28}\text{Si}$, $^{29}\text{Si}$ and $^{30}\text{Si}$.

|  | $^{28}\text{Si}$ | $^{29}\text{Si}$ | $^{30}\text{Si}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| relative isotopic mass | 28.0 | 29.0 | 30.0 |

A sample of silicon contains 92.2% $^{28}\text{Si}$. The total percentage abundance of $^{29}\text{Si}$ and $^{30}\text{Si}$ in the sample is 7.8%.

The relative atomic mass, $A_r$, of silicon in the sample is 28.09.

Calculate the percentage abundance of $^{30}\text{Si}$.

Give your answer to **one** decimal place.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Silicon reacts with nitrogen gas to form $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$.

$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ is a solid with a melting point of $1900^{\circ}\text{C}$. It is insoluble in water and does not conduct electricity when molten.

Suggest the type of bonding in **and** structure of $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Sulfur-containing compounds, such as $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{SH}$, are found in fossil fuels, and produce $\text{SO}_2$ when they are burned.
parts.text: Write the equation to show the complete combustion of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{SH}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State why the presence of $\text{SO}_2$ in the atmosphere has environmental consequences. Describe **one** of the consequences on the environment.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{SO}_2$ can react with ozone, $\text{O}_3$, to form $\text{SO}_3$ in two different reactions.
parts.text:
In one reaction, $\text{SO}_2$ reacts with $\text{O}_3$ until a dynamic equilibrium is established.

$$\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_3(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{SO}_3(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

State and explain the effect of an increase in pressure on the composition of the equilibrium mixture.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
In the other reaction, a different equilibrium is established at $300\text{ K}$ as shown.

$$3\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_3(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{SO}_3(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H = +462.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Suggest a temperature needed to increase the yield of $\text{SO}_3$ at equilibrium.

Explain your answer.
